\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{بچپن} (bachpan)}{بچپن (bachpan)}]{\ur{بچپن} (bachpan) — childhood}

\label{lesson:UR-C485-bachpan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to feed, then the Urdu for to give (someone) a drink.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{بچپن}}
\textbf{\ur{بچپن}} — \emph{bachpan} — \textquotedblleft{}childhood\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{بچپن} \ur{میں} \ur{میں} \ur{روز} \ur{پارک} \ur{جاتا} \ur{تھا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bachpan meṅ maiṅ roz pārk jātā thā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
As a child I went to the park every day.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{بچپن}} (\emph{bachpan}) is built on \textbf{\ur{بچہ}}, \textquotedblleft{}a child\textquotedblright{}, usually traced to Persian \emph{bachcha}, with the Indo-Aryan ending \emph{-pan}, \textquotedblleft{}-hood\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bachpan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bachpan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bachpan meṅ maiṅ roz pārk jātā thā.} — As a child I went to the park every day.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to feed, then the Urdu for to give (someone) a drink, then say \emph{bachpan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{بچپن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Childhood\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{شرارت} (sharārat)}{شرارت (sharārat)}]{\ur{شرارت} (sharārat) — mischief}

\label{lesson:UR-C485-shararat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to give (someone) a drink, then the Urdu for childhood.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{شرارت}}
\textbf{\ur{شرارت}} — \emph{sharārat} — \textquotedblleft{}mischief\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{بچے} \ur{کلاس} \ur{میں} \ur{شرارت} \ur{کر} \ur{رہے} \ur{تھے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bachche klās meṅ sharārat kar rahe the.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The children were up to mischief in class.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{شرارت}} (\emph{sharārat}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{sharāra}, \textquotedblleft{}wickedness\textquotedblright{}; in Urdu it is mostly a child's mischief.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sharārat}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bachche klās meṅ sharārat kar rahe the.} — The children were up to mischief in class.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to give (someone) a drink, then the Urdu for childhood, then say \emph{sharārat} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{توتلا} (totlā)}{توتلا (totlā)}]{\ur{توتلا} (totlā) — lisping; speaking like a small child}

\label{lesson:UR-C485-totla}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for childhood, then the Urdu for mischief.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{توتلا}}
\textbf{\ur{توتلا}} — \emph{totlā} — \textquotedblleft{}lisping; speaking like a small child\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{چھوٹا} \ur{بچہ} \ur{توتلی} \ur{زبان} \ur{میں} \ur{بولتا} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{chhoṭā bachchā totlī zabān meṅ boltā hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The little child talks in baby talk.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{توتلا}} (\emph{totlā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{totlā} under \emph{tōtta}, \textquotedblleft{}stammering\textquotedblright{}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 5965).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{پلنا} (palnā)}{پلنا (palnā)}]{\ur{پلنا} (palnā) — to be brought up}

\label{lesson:UR-C485-palna-reared}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for mischief, then the Urdu for lisping.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{پلنا}}
\textbf{\ur{پلنا}} — \emph{palnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to be brought up\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{وہ} \ur{دادی} \ur{کے} \ur{گھر} \ur{میں} \ur{پلی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{voh dādī ke ghar meṅ palī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She was brought up in her grandmother's house.
\end{quote}

Past (he …): \ur{وہ} \ur{نانی} \ur{کے} \ur{پاس} \ur{پلا}, \emph{voh nānī ke pās palā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{پلنا}} (\emph{palnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{palnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to be reared\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{pāláyati}, \textquotedblleft{}protects\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 8129); \textbf{\ur{پالنا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to bring up\textquotedblright{}, is its partner.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{palnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{voh dādī ke ghar meṅ palī.} — She was brought up in her grandmother's house.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for mischief, then the Urdu for lisping, then say \emph{palnā} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{پہنانا} (pahnānā)}{پہنانا (pahnānā)}]{\ur{پہنانا} (pahnānā) — to dress (someone)}

\label{lesson:UR-C485-pahnana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for lisping, then the Urdu for to be brought up.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{پہنانا}}
\textbf{\ur{پہنانا}} — \emph{pahnānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to dress (someone)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ماں} \ur{نے} \ur{بیٹی} \ur{کو} \ur{نیا} \ur{کرتا} \ur{پہنایا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{māṅ ne beṭī ko nayā kurtā pahnāyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The mother dressed her daughter in a new kurta.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{بچے} \ur{کو} \ur{جوتا} \ur{پہنایا}, \emph{us ne bachche ko jūtā pahnāyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{پہنانا}} (\emph{pahnānā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{pahnānā}, \textquotedblleft{}to clothe\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{pinahati}, \textquotedblleft{}ties on\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 8198); \textbf{\ur{پہننا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to wear\textquotedblright{}, is its partner.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pahnānā}, once more

\end{itemize}
